Manage difficulties positively, openly, courageously and ethically

At a glance

  • Address problems early rather than letting them escalate.
  • Speak honestly about concerns while maintaining respect.
  • Create safety for people to raise issues freely.
  • Act with courage, fairness and professional values.

Compassionate leadership means facing challenges directly rather than avoiding them. When difficulties are handled withopenness, fairness and courage , teams feel safer, conflicts are resolved earlier, and trust grows across the organisation.

Teams that manage difficulties positively, openly, courageously and ethically:

  • Address problems early instead of allowing them to escalate.
  • Speak honestly about concerns while maintaining respect and kindness.
  • Create a safe environment where people can raise issues without fear.
  • Make decisions guided by fairness, transparency and professional values.
  • Support one another through challenges and learn from difficult experiences.

Putting into practice

1. Create psychological safety

  • Encourage team members to raise concerns or mistakes without blame.
  • Respond calmly and constructively when issues are shared.
  • Reinforce that speaking up helps everyone improve.

2. Address problems early

  • Notice early signs of tension or confusion.
  • Initiate timely conversations rather than waiting for issues to worsen.
  • Use open questions to understand all perspectives.

3. Communicate openly and respectfully

  • Share concerns in a clear, kind and solution-focused way.
  • Avoid assumptions by checking facts and intentions.
  • Be transparent about decisions and the reasons behind them.

4. Act with courage and fairness

  • Support small tests of change rather than large-scale overhauls.
  • Give teams permission to try new approaches safely.
  • Share learning across teams so successful ideas spread more widely.

5. Remove barriers to improvement

  • Offer empathy and practical help when individuals or teams are struggling.
  • Recognise emotional strain and create space for people to talk.
  • Provide follow-up support to ensure improvements are sustained.

6. Reflect and learn after difficulties

  • Review what happened and what could be improved next time.
  • Encourage the team to contribute learning points and ideas.
  • Use insights to strengthen relationships, systems and ways of working.
